LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing, part of Strand 6 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why are idioms important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. mention idioms commonly used in the locality with peers,

2. listen to an audio recording on a creative story,

3. list idioms from the audio story,

4. discuss the meaning of various idioms used in the locality,

5. use idioms to write creative stories collaboratively,

6. read their creative stories in class for peer review,

7. team up with peers to publish their best stories in the school magazine or public magazines.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. mention idioms commonly used in the locality with peers,
2. listen to an audio recording on a creative story,
3. list idioms from the audio story,
4. discuss the meaning of various idioms used in the locality,
5. use idioms to write creative stories collaboratively,
6. read their creative stories in class for peer review,
7. team up with peers to publish their best stories in the school magazine or public magazines.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner engages actively to share their ideas and opinions on

meanings of various idioms.

• Creativity and Imagination: This is cultivated as the learner uses idioms to write own creative stories.

36

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner displays patience when reading their creative stories in class for peer review.

• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner strives to achieve a common goal as they team up to publish their best stories in the

school magazine or public magazines.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: This is enhanced as the learner accommodates people from special and vulnerable groups in the community.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of idioms to their learning of similar concepts in English.
